      <title>Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts?  | Andrew Beasley</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/michael-carrick-manchester-united-favourite-premier-league-sack-race</link>
      <description><p>Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away</p><p>No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change.</p><p>The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/michael-carrick-manchester-united-favourite-premier-league-sack-race">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Buildup to Sunday’s action, with a bumper WSL fixture list before Liverpool host Arsenal in the Premier League</p><p><strong>It is not going well for Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest, to say the least.</strong></p><p>“For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation that the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.”</p><p>Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said: “I don’t think they are not aware of the situation. We are exposed this season with this busy schedule, it’s really demanding.</p><p>“Is it unexpected? I don’t think so. Many clubs last year experienced exactly the same situation. First year in Europe, you know you will have on average 10 less points.
